guidelines.detail: refines FID-02 (The description distinguishes activity that occurs throughout the process from cancellation, which happens only if the customer decides to cancel. The generated flow makes the ongoing activity an unconditional predecessor of the cancellation event. This refines FID-02 by specifying how to preserve dependencies when activities have distinct timing.)

same as LRN-015 (The description distinguishes the customer submitting a cancellation request from the support team processing it, while the paired labels point to different actions and actors. LRN-015 already advises preserving materially stated actions and participants in labels, so this guideline expresses the same principle.)

same as LRN-010 (The description identifies a participant action that starts the process. The generated model uses a start event with that action’s label (X1), while the reference has a separate task for it (M3). This matches the learned guideline LRN-010.)

same as LRN-015 (The description distinguishes who submits a request from who processes it, and specifies multiple possible adjustments and outcome details; the generated labels show semantic divergence from those stated details. This is already covered essentially by learned guideline LRN-015.)

same as LRN-010 (The description states that the customer signs up to begin the process, while the records show the generated model used that action as a start event instead of modeling it as a task before account generation. This supports the already learned guideline LRN-010.)

same as LRN-015 (The label pairs show differences in preserved actions and scope, while the description confirms the relevant details. This guideline is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-015.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an activity occurs repeatedly or continues over an ongoing process and separately states that another activity starts only when a condition occurs: do not model the ongoing activity as an unconditional predecessor of the condition-triggered activity; preserve their distinct timing and stated dependencies in the BPMN flow
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an activity occurs repeatedly or continues over an ongoing process and separately states that another activity starts only when a condition occurs

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns distinct actions to different actors or describes separate actions at different stages of a process.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a process begins when a participant performs an identifiable action that establishes the process trigger: Model a start event for the trigger, followed by a separate task for the participant’s action; do not represent the action only as a start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant performs an identifiable action that initiates the process
